10 Two railway trucks of masses m and 3m move towards each other in opposite directions with
speeds 2v and v respectively. These trucks collide and stick together.
What is the speed of the trucks after the collision?
A
4
v
B
2
v
C
v
D
4
5v

hints: Notice the trucks move towards each other, so their velocities have opposite signs even though speeds $2v$ and $v$ are given as positive.
Compare the momentum magnitudes: $m \times 2v = 2mv$ versus $3m \times v = 3mv$ - the heavier truck has more momentum.
Set total initial momentum equal to $(m+3m)V$ for the stuck-together mass $4m$ and solve for the magnitude of $V$.
walkthrough: Take the direction of the mass $m$ as positive. Then its velocity is $+2v$ and the velocity of mass $3m$ is $-v$ because it moves oppositely.
Use conservation of linear momentum: total momentum before equals total momentum after, $p = mv$ with signs.
Total momentum before is $p_{initial} = m(2v) + 3m(-v) = 2mv - 3mv = -mv$. The negative sign means net momentum is in the original direction of the $3m$ truck.
After sticking, combined mass is $m + 3m = 4m$ moving with velocity $V$. So $p_{final} = 4mV$.
Speed is the magnitude, so speed $= v/4$. This is option A.

A.explanation: Total momentum $m(2v) - 3m(v) = -mv$ divided by combined mass $4m$ gives speed $v/4$.

B.explanation: Gives half the correct value, from an error in adding the opposite momenta or in dividing by $4m$.

C.explanation: Ignores vector signs and mass weighting, treating the $v$ of the $3m$ truck as the final speed.

D.explanation: Adds magnitudes $2mv + 3mv = 5mv$ without opposite signs, then divides by $4m$ to get $5v/4$.
